title: Wars for the West
objective: After this level you can explain the wars between the US Army and the Plains nations, from Little Bighorn in 1876 to Wounded Knee in 1890.
summary: The US recognized the Black Hills as Sioux land in 1868, then gold brought miners and war. The Lakota and allies beat Custer in 1876; at Wounded Knee in 1890 soldiers killed about 150 to 300 Lakota.

cards.headline: In 1876 the Lakota beat Custer at the Little Bighorn. In 1890 came Wounded Knee.
cards.body: Between those dates, the Plains nations fought to keep their homelands. The story starts with a promise about some hills.

cards.headline: A promise, then gold
cards.body: In the Fort Laramie Treaty of 1868, the United States recognized the Black Hills as part of the Great Sioux Reservation. Then, in 1874, George Armstrong Custer led an expedition into the Black Hills. Gold was found, and miners poured in. The government ordered the Lakota back to reservations by January 31, 1876, or be treated as hostile. A treaty is a promise on paper. Gold turned out to be heavier.

cards.headline: The Little Bighorn
cards.body: The Lakota and Northern Cheyenne were Plains nations. On June 25, 1876, at the Little Bighorn, Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho fighters under Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse defeated Custer. He and every soldier who followed him into the battle were killed. The victory was stunning, and short: the army flooded the region and forced the bands to surrender.

cards.headline: Wounded Knee
cards.body: By 1890 the Lakota faced hunger and a shrinking reservation, and some turned to the Ghost Dance, a religion that alarmed some US officials. On December 29, 1890, at Wounded Knee Creek, the 7th Cavalry killed about 150 to 300 Lakota, almost half of them women and children.
cards.callout: Estimates of the dead at Wounded Knee range from about 150 to 300

cards.headline: The claim that stayed
cards.body: The Lakota never dropped their claim to the Black Hills. In 1980 the Supreme Court ruled that the land had been taken and payment was owed. The Sioux refused the money. They wanted the land.

cards.headline: Wars for the West: explained

Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse beat Custer in 1876

questions.prompt: What happened at Wounded Knee Creek on December 29, 1890?

options.label: Sitting Bull’s fighters defeated Custer
options.rationale: That was the Little Bighorn, in 1876.

options.label: The 7th Cavalry killed about 150 to 300 Lakota
The Fort Laramie Treaty was signed
Miners found gold in the Black Hills

questions.explanation: At Wounded Knee, the 7th Cavalry killed about 150 to 300 Lakota, almost half of them women and children.

questions.prompt: Put these events in the fight for the Black Hills in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: The Fort Laramie Treaty came in 1868 and Custer’s expedition in 1874. The Little Bighorn was fought in 1876, Wounded Knee came in 1890, and the Supreme Court ruled on the Black Hills in 1980.

questions.prompt: Among Level 3’s culture areas, the Lakota and Northern Cheyenne belonged to _____.
questions.explanation: The Lakota and Northern Cheyenne were Plains nations, and the Plains is one of Level 3’s culture areas.
